promise: You fight the Owing, a humane native debt-labour custom that drifted into inherited bondage, by freeing its people and burying its dead, and you pay for each win.
core: Injustice with no villain: correct arithmetic, kind brokers and a ruin that is implicated rather than evil. Burial work and abolition work are the same work.
identity: The Blackrose Chainbreakers, who oppose the Owing (debt labour counted in nushmeekos). The tell is washed-out colour and markings from distance from the Hist. Always give the Owing defenders it has genuinely served.
free: Which estate, crossing or dock hosts each case, minor workers and witnesses, ledger contents beyond the stated arithmetic, route of the procession.

promise: Eight strange, standalone encounters, one per Prince plus the unexplained, that feel like intrusions of Oblivion into a Hist-and-Sithis world and leave at least one thing unexplained.
core: Wonder and unease: each Prince's bargain is technically intact and practically ruinous, and the choice is the player's, with Argonians reacting from their own cosmology rather than as followers of the Princes.
free: Which settlement or ruin hosts each quest, minor cast names, route and set dressing, which of the eight sit in Milestone 1 (DQ01-DQ04) versus wave 2, and which vanilla artifact mesh is re-skinned as the reward.

promise: Join a band of crime solvers in Black Marsh and climb from petty thefts and larcenies through murder mysteries to a grand murder finale involving highly important people of the province.
core: Solving crimes the Shadowscales (assassins) and the Night-Reed Chapter (thieves) live by, using classic mystery structures made to fit the lore and the world.
identity: A joinable faction of crime solvers, rival to the Shadowscales and the Night-Reed Chapter. Its name, founding, patrons, headquarters and the lore reason someone would pay for and trust detectives are still to come from a lore pass; not yet written.
free: Almost everything is open: the faction's name, founding, patrons, headquarters, ranks, number of cases per rank, the cast, which regions host cases, and the finale's victim and culprit. Fixed by the decision only: escalation by case, a joinable faction, rivalry with the two guilds, a grand finale with important NPCs, grounded in lore and in simple classic mystery structures.
source: docs/decisions/0025-a-detectives-faction.md; story/design/narrative-lines.md; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md (§3 crime and the shadow); story/lore/topics/sithis-nisswo-shadowscales.md

promise: You stand up for people the old tribal and Hist order has no place for, and every victory sharpens the question of who a free city is really for.
core: Citizenship, property and plural identity, and the risk that openness turns into rule by wealth.
identity: A civic faction of Lukiul, mixed-city citizens, merchants, workers and reformers seeking civic standing independent of tribe or Hist. Ranks: Petitioner, Advocate, Ward Delegate, charter branch office.
free: Which city hosts each case, minor people, street and building layouts, route names, market and warehouse dressing, the names of blocs and officials other than the named ones (Advocate Oshu-Kai).
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md:section 38 The League of Open Water; story/lore/topics/hist-and-sap.md; story/lore/regions/shadowfen.md

promise: The province feels lived in: each place has its own problem that comes from its ground, water, history and people, not from a hero's errand.
core: Local trouble is caused by real arrangements (tolls, rites, debts, records, stone and water) and the player settles it by reading them, with choices that favour some people over others.
free: Which places host which quest, the names of minor people, routes, set dressing and the order of regional packets; skeleton premises may be reshaped as long as the shape of the problem survives.

promise: A nobody pulled out of a burnt camp, owed to no one, becomes the spy the Veiled Reed can deny and the treasure-hunter who finds the Eye of Argonia before the Unbound Root does: through smugglers' docks, a drowned prison, a wreck, a sunken Xanmeer and the lethal basin to the Lost City and the door in the sap-dreams, where the player holds the jewel and chooses what Black Marsh keeps.
core: A hunt and a spy story in the marsh: every quest is a place to reach, a thing to find, a cut tree to read, a cell to outrun or outfight, won with the player's own skills. The Hist and the sap are the mystery; the cult's grievance is real and its severance indiscriminate; the Reed's secrets have victims. Law, custom and the state's paper stay in the background.
free: Which BM&V cell or building hosts a beat (fitted at record time, "Places to fit at record time"); names of minor people; routes and boats; set dressing; levels and placements (nothing levelled against the player). Choices do not multiply: each quest works the same whatever came before; only the finale's CUT, CLAIM or MEND carries forward.
source: story/design/quests/main-line-outline.md; story/design/quests/30-main-quest.md §16, §18, §19, §23, §24; story/design/quests/review/act1.md (the whole main line, rounds 1 to 6); story/lore/eye-of-argonia.md; story/lore/topics/hist-and-sap.md; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md; story/lore/topics/sithis-nisswo-shadowscales.md

promise: You are the one who goes into the danger and finds the truth, then stands in council and decides what it is worth. Every hearing pays off something won underwater, upriver or inside someone's work camp.
core: Consent, stewardship and the limits of traditional authority: no Hist speaks for all Hist, and every remedy benefits some residents at the cost of others.
identity: Tree-Minders and Hist communities mediating ecology, eggs, sap, roads and local autonomy without assuming one voice. Ranks Helper, Root-Walker, Community Mediator, branch Conclave office. Plural and reform branches coexist; hardline closed leadership conflicts with senior Open Water League office.
free: Which Hist settlement, grove, channel or dock hosts each quest; names of minor people; exact routes and hazard points; set dressing. The mid-line procedure choice and the end states must stay.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 36 The Many-Root Conclave; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Many-Root; story/lore/topics/hist-and-sap.md; story/lore/topics/hist-placement.md

promise: You take paid, practical defence work in a swamp frontier and discover that who is protected, and who is billed, is the real contract.
core: Professional competence versus exploitation, public service, ecology, and whether accepting a charter means becoming foreign.
identity: A native martial tradition (Four Winds of Stonewastes, shellback levies, kaals, hired village defenders) arguing over accepting a foreign chartered form; explicitly not a Fighters Guild branch. Ranks: Recruit, Proven Blade, Contract Captain, charter branch office.
free: Villages, forts and creature habitats used, minor officers, trophy and ledger details, exact routes, which old guild hall is reused.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md:section 33 The Marsh Charter; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md (cited in section 33)

promise: You rise from proving yourself on a small recovery to a province-famous heist on Lilmoth's Crown Ledger, and then decide who owns the night.
core: Skill and loyalty among the dispossessed, professional restraint, criminal mutual aid, and the pull of blackmail power.
identity: A native Argonian thieves guild (not an Imperial franchise) adapted to canals, boats, flooded districts and rootworm routes. Ranks Lookout, Cutpurse, Water-Rat, Night-Reed, senior branch outcome. No Nocturnal oath. Three desks with three ethics: Tilts-The-Jug at Soulrest (restraint), Vasha 'Half-Rent' at Lilmoth (leverage), Sails-By-Morning at Archon (velocity).
free: Which docks, dens, houses and mooring spots stand in; names of minor people and fences; tool and route details; the Archon fence den location. Palace and vault names may change with the world's own seat of government.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 32; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md section 3; story/lore/topics/ecology-encounters-loot.md section 2; story/design/quests/36-cast-roster.md section 56; story/design/quests/index/factions.md

promise: You learn a living Argonian tradition of death, change and mediation by taking part, and help decide whether it stays dispersed or builds a school.
core: Plural belief, grief, mercy and fraud, and the danger of turning change into dogma. You end as a respected interpreter, not an unquestioned prophet.
identity: A mainstream Argonian Sithis tradition focused on change, death, interpretation and community mediation, distinct from the Unbound Root. Ranks Listener, Path-Bearer, Interpreter, then regional teacher or itinerant elder by outcome.
free: Which shrines, platforms, homes and settlements are used, names of minor people, routes. The pilgrimage circuit in the authoring nudge is optional, to keep or drop on fit.

promise: A holding bin of unauthored ideas raised by the 2026-09-04 quest and world co-design pass; no promise to the player until an author picks one up.
core: Each proposal is a mystery or dispute grown out of a place in the plotted province (weirs, sluices, crossings, stations, stakes); the bin itself has no theme beyond that.
free: Everything: the whole line is unauthored and any row may be dropped, reshaped or merged.

promise: You run the water routes that keep Argonia moving, and decide whether the pilots' trade stays mutual aid or becomes a cartel.
core: Mobility, labour, monopoly and sacred routes, and the line between mutual aid and cartel power.
identity: The Reed-Sail Compact: pilots, ferries, boat crews, smugglers and dock workers. Ranks: Deckhand, Pilot, Route-Keeper, branch-specific officer. Includes a pirate branch (Salt-Teeth arc).
free: Docks, routes and hubs used, minor pilots and passengers, boat and cargo detail, cove and ship placement; the pirate-branch quests are concept and wave 2.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md:section 37 The Reed-Sail Compact and section 43 Salt-Teeth arc; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md

promise: You serve a small order that keeps the secret root-transit routes running, and decide what the order becomes.
core: Sacred routes and access: mutual aid against monopoly, safety against secrecy. The worm is never seen, only its effects.
identity: A handful of keepers on routes secret by doctrine; two fixed posts: Ki-Ossa at the Helstrom terminus (also the restrictionist voice) and Tuxo at the hidden station. Two desks by declared canon exception.
free: Station positions (the layout is a placeholder awaiting Hist-node placement), pen and cavern layouts, minor handlers, smuggler identities.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 42 Rootworm Waykeepers; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Rootworm Waykeepers; story/lore/topics/roads-and-routes-4e201.md

promise: You are drawn into the contest over reviving an order everyone wants and nobody made, and you decide what the Shadowscales become.
core: Duty, consent and political assassination: whether birth, tradition, state power or consent can recreate a real order, or only a useful costume.
identity: A dead assassin order (training facility shut 4E 187, last known Shadowscale dies 4E 201) with four bidders: Dark Brotherhood, Black-Tongues, the Veiled Reed state, and an independent ethical order. Ranks Watcher, Knife-Bearer, Writ-Keeper, senior branch office; leadership only in the independent branch, answerable to a council.
free: Where the ruined facility, hatchery, safehouses, courthouse and meeting rooms sit, names of minor people, rooftop and canal routes, which city fabric is reused. The design says not to build a province-scale assassin network.

promise: You work among scholars and custodians who all want a piece of what lies under the water, and you decide whose knowledge it is and what gets published.
core: Ownership of knowledge, research ethics, translation, and the political force of archives, with the fight over whether such a body should become an institution at all.
identity: Black Marsh scholars between local custodians, the Synod and the College of Whispers after the Mages Guild's fall. Not robed mages: tree-minders, alchemists, grave-singers, jekka-wats, bone-workers and a few foreign-trained scholars. Spine is the Conclave of Baal at Stormhold. Ranks Copyist, Field Reader, Custodian, branch-aligned senior scholar. Synod, College and independent endings are mutually exclusive.
free: Which ruins, camps and offices host each quest; names of minor scholars; the choice of creature or construct; routes. Staffing must stay non-robed and local.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 34 The Sunken Archive; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Sunken Archive; story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md sections 1-2

promise: You help Argonian and Dunmer neighbours contain border violence without erasing slavery, invasion or living claims.
core: Competing memory and present economics: the hardest question (saltrice title) cuts across the ethnic line, not along it.
identity: The Thorn Ash-Reed Accord: Argonian and Dunmer residents of Thorn trying to contain border violence; both militias are the wrong shape for the real problems.
free: Neighbourhoods, field and dock locations, minor suspects and family names, militia room layouts.

promise: You handle an inherited catastrophe that nobody alive saw, and decide how the truth of Umbriel is kept, told or buried.
core: History argued over at the distance of inherited memory: edited testimony, missing households, and a Society whose own founding account is compromised.
identity: Inheritors and archivists, not survivors. Desks: Keeps-The-Count at the Lilmoth archive room, Neexa-Tul behind a Pusbottom chandlery (the dead belong to families; testimony may be consulted, never kept; write one line of your own family's before reading), and Old Nusa at Deepmire.
free: Archive, home and workshop locations; names of minor people; the route and shelters of the UW04 trek, provided it remains the line's one traversal spike.
source: story/design/quests/40-factions.md section 41 Umbriel Witness Society; story/design/quests/index/factions.md Umbriel Witness; story/lore/topics/umbriel.md; story/lore/extrapolation/argonia-4e201-state.md section 9
